title: Show a meeting to attendees and move it between offices

blocks.text: The scheduling service stores each meeting as a `ZonedDateTime` in the zone of the office that hosts it. Two tickets are open. Attendees in other offices say the invite email shows the meeting at the wrong time for them; one in Toronto joined a Madrid meeting long after it had ended. And when an organiser hands a recurring 16:30 meeting to the office in another country, the new office finds it at some other hour of their day.

items: `asSeenBy(meeting, attendeeZone)`: the meeting as an attendee living in `attendeeZone` finds it in their calendar;
`moveToOffice(meeting, officeZone)`: the meeting once the office in `officeZone` hosts it, at the same time on its clocks as before.

blocks.text: `inviteLines` already builds the email from `asSeenBy`. About two lines in total.

cases.says: between two zones whose clocks agree, the attendee's view and the moved meeting both keep the time
the invite has one line per attendee, in the order given
an attendee in another zone sees the same moment on their own clock, on another date if the date line lies between
when only one of the two zones has changed its clocks, the attendee's time uses the offsets in force on the meeting's date
a meeting moved to another office keeps its time on the clock, which makes it a different moment

origin.section: withZoneSameInstant Converts a Moment; withZoneSameLocal Moves It

concepts: withZoneSameInstant keeps the moment and recomputes the wall clock; withZoneSameLocal keeps the wall clock and so changes the moment.
The difference between two zones depends on the date, because they change their clocks on different days, so it can't be a constant.
